spark.scene: True-color view of the main Hawaiian Islands chain from the northwest to the large island in the southeast. Dark open ocean dominates the center with scattered white cumulus to the north, extensive white cloud decks to the southwest and east, and white orographic clouds covering much of the large island.

per_plume.source_hint: open ocean southwest of Hawaii Island; no vent or fire attachment identified
evidence: USGS HVO status at image time shows Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW in episodic_pause after episode 55 fountaining ended yesterday, and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so no sustained eruptive vog source. [E1]
FIRMS shows no fire clusters in the Hawaii box, only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal glow, arguing against wildfire_smoke for this ocean veil. [E3]

Plume is not attached to a vent: wind-based upwind end is ~101.9 km from Kilauea and ~68.2 km from Mauna Loa, and tracked source end is in open ocean ~219.7 km from Kilauea and ~188.7 km from Mauna Loa. [E6, E5]

Measured 3-h drift toward 93 deg east disagrees by ~77 deg with wind-implied transport toward ~170 deg from 350 deg northerly wind, exceeding 45 deg tolerance and lowering confidence; fit R2 0.56. [E5, E2]

Mask is mostly ocean (land_frac 0.195) with no island swallowed, so not a land artifact, but very faint pale blue-gray veil amid extensive SW and E white cloud decks leaves thin cloud contamination possible. [E4]

classify.caveats: Very faint veil in partly cloudy scene with extensive white decks nearby; Kilauea in episodic pause not actively fountaining; measured drift disagrees with wind and neither geometric nor tracked source end attaches to a vent.

kilauea.activity_summary: The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is currently paused after episode 55 fountaining ended yesterday at 9:03 a.m. HST. Summit reinflation continues today following the end of the fountaining.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
